subject: Physics
title: Core 1B Phenomenological Reconstruction Cycles & Cognitive Dissonance Dialog: Kinematics

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Split-Distance Average Speed & Harmonic Mean Invariant
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: A particle covers distance d at speed v1 and the subsequent equal distance d at speed v2. The elapsed times are t1 = d / v1 and t2 = d / v2. Total distance is 2d and total time is t1 + t2. Average speed is v_avg = 2d / (d/v1 + d/v2) = 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2).

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Instead of weighting by distance, weight by elapsed time. Average speed is the time-weighted average: v_avg = (v1*t1 + v2*t2) / (t1 + t2). Because t = d / v, the traveler inevitably spends more time creeping at the slower speed than sprinting at the higher speed.
phenomenological_reconstruction.dominant_regime: The slower speed dominates the time budget; therefore, the average speed must always lie strictly closer to the minimum speed than to the maximum speed.
phenomenological_reconstruction.arithmetic_contrast: The arithmetic mean (v1 + v2)/2 represents equal time allocation, which is structurally unattainable when distance intervals are matched.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: v_avg -> 0 (Total time diverges to infinity; trip is never completed)
v_avg -> 2*v1 (Average speed is strictly bounded by twice the slower speed)

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Parabolic Symmetry & Dual-Time Product Measuring Height
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: From 1D constant-acceleration free fall: h = u*t - 0.5*g*t^2 => 0.5*g*t^2 - u*t + h = 0. Solving via quadratic formula yields roots t1, t2 = (u +- sqrt(u^2 - 2gh)) / g. The sum of roots is t1 + t2 = 2u / g = T (total flight time), and the product of roots is t1 * t2 = 2h / g => h = 0.5 * g * t1 * t2.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Shift the temporal origin to the apex turnaround instant t_apex = u / g. At the apex, vertical velocity is exactly zero.
phenomenological_reconstruction.ascent_descent_matching: The climb from height h to apex takes time Delta t = sqrt(u^2 - 2gh) / g. By time-reversal symmetry of conservative gravitational acceleration, the descent from apex back to h takes the identical duration Delta t.
phenomenological_reconstruction.root_decomposition: Thus, the two passage times decompose as t1 = t_apex - Delta t and t2 = t_apex + Delta t. Adding them yields t1 + t2 = 2*t_apex = T. Multiplying them yields t1*t2 = t_apex^2 - (Delta t)^2 = (u/g)^2 - (u^2 - 2gh)/g^2 = 2h/g, directly proving h = 0.5*g*t1*t2 without quadratic formula memorization.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: t1 = t2 = u/g (Apex coincidence; discriminant vanishes)
t1 = 0 and t2 = T = 2u/g (Launch and landing)
Roots become complex; physically unattainable height

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Free-Fall Elevator Equivalence of Dropped vs Fired Projectiles
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Dropped ball has y1(t) = h - 0.5*g*t^2. Horizontally fired projectile has y2(t) = h - 0.5*g*t^2 and x2(t) = u*t. For both particles, the ground landing condition is y(T) = 0 => T = sqrt(2h/g), identical for both regardless of horizontal launch speed u.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Step inside an imaginary elevator falling freely alongside the cliff edge with acceleration g.
phenomenological_reconstruction.effective_gravity: Inside this frame, real gravity g is exactly cancelled by the upward inertial pseudo-acceleration -g. The effective gravity is g_eff = 0.
phenomenological_reconstruction.motion_in_elevator: Inside the elevator, the dropped ball is in static rest. The fired projectile travels in a uniform horizontal straight line at constant velocity u with zero vertical deflection.
phenomenological_reconstruction.floor_motion: The ground floor is accelerating upward at g toward the elevator with speed v_floor(t) = g*t. The upward rushing floor impacts both the stationary ball and the horizontally gliding projectile at the exact same instant, proving identical drop time.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: T -> infinity; particles glide horizontally and remain suspended

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Zero-Acceleration Relative Frame of Two Free Projectiles
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Particle 1: r1(t) = u1*t + 0.5*g*t^2. Particle 2: r2(t) = r2_0 + u2*t + 0.5*g*t^2. The relative position vector is r_rel(t) = r1(t) - r2(t) = -r2_0 + (u1 - u2)*t. Relative acceleration is a_rel = g - g = 0.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Ride on particle 2. Because both particles experience the identical acceleration vector g, this common acceleration cancels out completely from the relative equation of motion.
phenomenological_reconstruction.rectified_path: Seen from particle 2, particle 1 travels along an exact straight line with constant vector velocity v_rel = u1 - u2.
phenomenological_reconstruction.collision_criterion: Collision occurs if and only if the constant relative velocity vector v_rel points directly along the initial line-of-sight vector r2_0 - r1_0.
phenomenological_reconstruction.shortest_distance: The shortest distance of approach between the two projectiles is simply the perpendicular distance from particle 2 to the straight line of relative motion: d_min = |r2_0 x v_rel| / |v_rel|.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: v_rel = 0; separation distance remains strictly constant for all t
d_min = 0; collision is inevitable regardless of gravity

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: At the highest point of a vertical throw, the ball stops moving, so its acceleration must be zero.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: If acceleration were zero at the top when velocity is zero, what would happen to its velocity in the next millisecond? By definition, Delta v = a * Delta t = 0 * Delta t = 0. Would the ball remain suspended frozen in the sky?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Because acceleration is the non-zero rate of change dv/dt = -9.8 m/s^2, the velocity does not remain zero; it immediately shifts from 0 to negative values, pulling the ball downward.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: Driving half the distance at 40 km/h and half at 60 km/h gives an average speed of 50 km/h.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: Suppose the trip is 120 km total (60 km each half). At 40 km/h, the first half takes 1.5 hours. At 60 km/h, the second half takes 1.0 hour. Total time is 2.5 hours. What is 120 km divided by 2.5 hours?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: 120 / 2.5 = 48 km/h! The driver spent 1.5 hours at 40 km/h and only 1.0 hour at 60 km/h. Slower travel consumes more time, lowering the average speed below the arithmetic mean.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: A high-speed bullet fired horizontally stays airborne longer because its high velocity opposes gravity.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: Which force opposes gravity along the vertical axis? Is there any upward lift or vertical aerodynamic force in a vacuum?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: None! Gravity acts strictly downward (-g j) and has zero component horizontally. The bullet falls vertically at the exact same rate as a dropped coin.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: A negative velocity on a motion graph always means the object is decelerating (slowing down).
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: If a ball is falling downward at -20 m/s and one second later is moving at -30 m/s, is its speed increasing or decreasing? What is the sign of its velocity?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Speed is the absolute magnitude |v|: it increased from 20 m/s to 30 m/s! The object is speeding up in the negative direction. Deceleration only occurs when velocity and acceleration have opposite signs.
